name: Shipeach – Per Product Shipping for WooCommerce
author: Emtiaz Zahid

sections.description:
Shipeach adds per product shipping to WooCommerce: set a shipping cost on each product and each variation, by country, state or postcode, and WooCommerce charges it, either as its own shipping method in your zones or on top of your other shipping methods. It is for stores where shipping depends on the item rather than the cart: furniture, art, plants, bulky or fragile goods, drop-shipped items with supplier-set shipping. It does not fetch carrier rates, print labels or pack boxes.

Shipeach is an independent plugin and is not affiliated with WooCommerce or Automattic.

Features

  • Rules on every product. Under Product data → Shipping, below the shipping class, tick “Per-product shipping” and add rules: Country (any or one country), State (any, a state from WooCommerce’s list, or a code for countries without a list), Postcode, a line cost charged once per cart line and an item cost charged per unit. Add and remove rows without reloading the page. Up to 200 rules per product.
  • Postcodes like shipping zones. A postcode can be exact (SW1A 1AA), a wildcard (PE*) or a range (1000-1999 or 1000...1999). They are matched with the same WooCommerce function shipping zones use. A hyphen between two numbers of the same length, lower number first, is read as a range.
  • Variation overrides. Each variation has an “Override shipping rules” checkbox and its own table. When it is ticked, the variation’s rules replace the parent product’s rules entirely; otherwise the variation uses the parent’s.
  • Most specific rule wins. A postcode rule beats a state rule, which beats a country rule, which beats an “any” rule. Between rules that are equally specific, the first row in the table wins.
  • “Per Product Shipping” zone method. Add it to any shipping zone. Settings: Title, Tax status, Default line cost and Default item cost (used for products with per-product shipping on but no rule matching the address), “Products without per-product shipping” (charge nothing for them, or do not offer the method), “Hide Free Shipping when this method applies” and “Hide Local Pickup when this method applies”. The rate is the sum of every line’s line cost plus item cost × quantity.
  • Or add the costs to your other methods. Under WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → Per Product Shipping, “Add per-product costs to every other shipping method” adds the package’s per-product cost to every other rate offered for the package, such as Flat rate. Free Shipping is never changed, Local Pickup is left unchanged unless you untick that option, and taxes are recalculated for taxable rates. The zone method and this option can be used together; the Per Product Shipping rate itself is not increased.
  • Breakdown on the order. The order’s shipping line stores which product cost what. The admin order screen shows it as “Per-product breakdown: Product A 9.00, Product B 4.00”. Customers do not see it.
  • Quick edit and bulk edit. From the products list, turn per-product shipping on or off and set the line and item cost of the “Any country” rule for one or many products.
  • Tools → Per Product Shipping. Copy the rules of one product or variation to other products and variations in one form, and see how many products use per-product shipping with a link to the products list filtered to them. The products list also gets a “Per-product shipping: on / off” filter.
  • WP-CLI. wp shipeach rules list [--product=<id>], wp shipeach rules set <product> --country= --state= --postcode= --line= --item=, wp shipeach rules import <file.csv> [--mode=replace|append] and wp shipeach rules export [--out=<file>].

How it works

  1. Open a product, go to Product data → Shipping, tick “Per-product shipping” and add one or more rules. For a variable product, add rules on the parent, and tick “Override shipping rules” on any variation that ships differently.
  2. Either add the “Per Product Shipping” method to a shipping zone (WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping), or turn on “Add per-product costs to every other shipping method” under WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → Per Product Shipping, or both.
  3. At checkout, every item in the package is matched against its rules for the shipping address. The matching rule’s line cost plus item cost × quantity is that line’s shipping, and the lines are added up.

Rates are calculated on the server, so the classic cart and checkout, the block cart and checkout, and the Store API all show the same amounts. When a product’s rules change, carts calculate fresh rates instead of reusing the ones stored in the customer’s session.

Compatibility

  • Classic and block cart and checkout, and the Store API. No JavaScript runs on the storefront.
  • High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS): compatibility is declared and the plugin runs no order queries.
  • Rules are ordinary product meta (_shipeach_enabled and _shipeach_rules), so WooCommerce’s “Duplicate” action copies them, and WooCommerce’s product CSV export and import carry them when “Export custom meta” is ticked.
  • Costs are entered in your store’s base currency. Multi-currency plugins can convert them with the shipeach_rule_cost filter.

Developers

Filters: shipeach_rules_for_product (the rules used for a cart item), shipeach_rule_matches (whether a rule applies, for example quantity or weight tiers), shipeach_rule_cost (the cost of one cart line), shipeach_package_cost (the total for a package), shipeach_import_rows (CSV rows before import).
Action: shipeach_after_import.
The order shipping line meta _shipeach_breakdown holds product or variation ID → cost.

sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce 8.0 or newer.
  2. Install Shipeach from the Plugins screen (or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/) and activate it.
  3. Add rules under Product data → Shipping on your products, then add the “Per Product Shipping” method to a shipping zone or turn on the option under WooCommerce → Settings → Shipping → Per Product Shipping.
sections.faq:
Can variations have their own shipping costs?

Yes. Tick “Override shipping rules” on the variation and add its rules. The variation’s rules then replace the parent product’s rules entirely, so an address that matches none of the variation’s rules gets the method’s default cost, not the parent’s rule. Variations without the override use the parent’s rules.

Does it work with the block cart and checkout?

Yes. Rates are calculated on the server by WooCommerce’s shipping API, so the block cart and checkout (and anything else using the Store API) show the same rate as the classic checkout. Compatibility with the cart and checkout blocks and with HPOS is declared.

Which rule is used when several match?

The most specific one: a postcode rule, then a state rule, then a country rule, then an “any” rule. If two matching rules are equally specific, the one higher in the table wins.

What happens to products without per-product shipping?

With the “Per Product Shipping” zone method, the “Products without per-product shipping” setting decides: “Charge nothing for them” (the default) adds nothing for those items, while “Do not offer this method” hides the method whenever the cart contains one, so your other methods apply. A product with per-product shipping on but no rule for the address is charged the method’s Default line cost and Default item cost (0 when left blank). When adding costs to other methods, items without a matching rule add nothing.

How does it work with Free Shipping and Local Pickup?

Adding per-product costs to other methods never changes Free Shipping rates, and leaves Local Pickup unchanged unless you untick “Leave Local Pickup rates unchanged”. The “Per Product Shipping” zone method has its own options to hide Free Shipping and Local Pickup whenever it is offered.

Does it work with multi-currency plugins?

Costs are entered and calculated in your store’s base currency. Shipeach does not convert them itself; a multi-currency plugin or a small snippet can convert each line’s cost with the shipeach_rule_cost filter.

How do I import rules from a CSV file?

With WP-CLI. Each line is one rule with six columns in this order: product ID (a variation ID is fine), country code, state code, postcode, line cost, item cost. A first line that does not start with a number is skipped as a header. * or an empty country, state or postcode means “any”, and an empty cost is 0. Run wp shipeach rules import rules.csv (each product’s rules are replaced by the rows given for it) or add --mode=append to add the rows after its existing rules. wp shipeach rules export writes all rules in the same format to the shipeach folder inside your uploads directory. The Tools screen does not upload files.

Can I use a CSV file from the WooCommerce.com Per Product Shipping extension?

Its documentation lists the same six columns in the same order (product ID, country code, state code, postcode, line cost, item cost), and the header line is skipped, so wp shipeach rules import reads that layout. Shipeach has not been tested with files exported by the extension itself, so review the imported rules afterwards. Also note that Shipeach uses the most specific matching rule, while that documentation says the first matching row from the top of the table is used.

Does Shipeach send anything to its author or to other services?

No. It makes no outbound requests and uses no external service. It charges the costs you enter; it does not fetch carrier rates, print labels or pack boxes.
